## Context / Problem

rebar is driven by MANY local agent processes at once — high local concurrency is the normal
operating mode, not an edge case. Concurrent rebar sessions contend on LOCAL git operations
against the shared tickets store (`.git/index.lock`, ref locks such as `HEAD.lock` /
`packed-refs.lock`), and today that contention surfaces as errors to the agent running the
command instead of being absorbed. Prior tickets bounded the NETWORK-capable call sites
(747f, 77e1, 983f) and fixed the store-lock identity/wedge class (304e, 5389); this ticket
covers the remaining class: local git call sites with no contention policy and (for several)
no bound at all — `_commands/compact.py`, `_commands/delete.py`, `_commands/fsck.py`,
`_commands/txn.py`, `_store/event_append.py`, `metrics/blame.py`, `metrics/git_metrics.py`.

The OSS research this ticket commissioned is recorded in the comments above and informs the
design (git lockfile.c's jittered backoff, Gitaly's lock knobs + watchdog deadlines, JGit's
own-lock-before-file-lock serialization, Mercurial's bounded wait, Bazel's "print the holder,
never parse it").

OPERATOR-RATIFIED DECISION (2026-08-04, recorded as a comment above): handle local git lock
contention AUTOMATICALLY, with NO escalation to the agent — a per-store advisory lock plus
bounded jittered retry/backoff on the store's git call sites (consistent with the existing
push-retry pattern in `rebar._store.push`); transient conflicts resolve silently (at most a
debug/warning log); only a genuinely stuck lock (bounded budget exhausted) surfaces one
actionable error naming the lock file with holder guidance. Defaults on the order of tens of
seconds, jittered; NO new config keys (no store/git config surface exists today).

## Approach

All changes at the store's local git execution seam so every routed call site inherits them:

1. **Per-store advisory git-op lock** (`rebar._store.gitutil`): `run_git_write` serializes the
   store's index-mutating git invocations across rebar processes with a kernel
   `fcntl.flock` on a per-store lock file inside the tracker's git dir. Fast path is a single
   non-blocking `flock` (zero added latency, no sleep, when uncontended). When contended, poll
   with short jittered sleeps up to a bounded budget, logging at debug. The kernel drops the
   lock when its holder dies, so there is NO staleness/reclamation logic to get wrong (the
   Bazel/cargo property cited in the research). On budget exhaustion, log a warning and
   proceed WITHOUT the advisory lock — it is a contention reducer; correctness stays with the
   git-level retry below (JGit's in-process fair lock pattern).
2. **Bounded jittered retry on git's own lock signatures** (`_with_index_lock_retry`):
   extend the retried signature from index.lock-only to git's ref/config lock conflicts
   ("cannot lock ref", "<name>.lock': File exists"); jitter every backoff sleep by
   uniform[0.75, 1.25] (git lockfile.c's exact shape, research §1a); raise the retry budget
   from ~2s to the order of tens of seconds (default ~20s summed backoff). Stale-index-lock
   reclamation semantics are unchanged and still apply only to index.lock.
3. **One actionable exhaustion error**: when the budget is exhausted and the failure is still
   a lock signature, the returned `CompletedProcess.stderr` is augmented with the lock file
   path (parsed from git's own message when present) and holder guidance ("held by another
   git process; if none is running, remove the lock file") — so every existing call site
   (txn/compact/delete raise `CommandError` from stderr) surfaces one actionable error with
   no per-site changes.
4. **Jitter the store write-lock contention sleeps** (`rebar._store.lock`): `_acquire_fcntl`
   (fixed 50ms) and `_acquire_mkdir` (fixed 100ms) get the same uniform[0.75, 1.25] jitter —
   research rec #4 (thundering-herd de-synchronization). Budgets/semantics unchanged.
5. **Watchdog bounds for the remaining local-only sites** (AC 2 of the original filing):
   `run_git_write` gets a generous local watchdog (120s, folded into a synthetic rc-124
   result exactly like `event_append._run_git`), covering txn/compact/delete;
   `fsck.py`'s read-only `_git` gets the same 120s fold; `metrics/blame.py` and
   `metrics/git_metrics.py` get 300s (research 5b rec 3: blame/log walks are legitimately
   slow, hold no store lock — watchdog-grade only). `event_append` keeps its existing 30s.
   These are watchdogs against a wedged filesystem/lock, NOT latency budgets — deliberately
   NOT copied from the 300s/30s network values but justified against local latency
   (research §2: "watchdog-grade bound is defensible; latency-grade is not").

Blocking policy under local contention, stated explicitly (AC 4 of the original filing):
**bounded jittered retry** — serialize rebar's own writers via the advisory lock, ride out
transient git lock conflicts silently with jittered backoff to a tens-of-seconds budget, and
fail with ONE actionable error only when the budget is exhausted (stuck lock). Chosen over
block-forever (cargo/Bazel) because rebar's callers are unattended agents with their own
deadlines, and over fail-fast because the observed conflicts resolve on retry.

No new config keys: constants are module-level (the established `_INDEX_LOCK_*` pattern) so
tests can tune them; no config surface for store/git behavior exists to extend.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py` — advisory lock, jitter helper, ref-lock signature, raised
  jittered budget, actionable exhaustion stderr, 120s watchdog in `run_git_write`
- `src/rebar/_store/lock.py` — jittered contention sleeps (two `time.sleep` call sites)
- `src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py` — bound its local `_git` wrapper (120s, rc-124 fold)
- `src/rebar/metrics/blame.py`, `src/rebar/metrics/git_metrics.py` — 300s watchdog
- `tests/interfaces/store/test_git_contention_9305.py` (new) — the RED-first behavioral suite
- existing tests under `tests/interfaces/store/` + `tests/unit/` adjusted only if the raised
  budget/jitter breaks a timing assumption

## Testing

STRICT TDD (operator condition): RED behavioral tests first, real git repos in tmp dirs with
a competing lock holder — behavioral/contractual, not change-detectors:

- (a) an index-mutating store git op hitting a transient `index.lock` held briefly by a
  competing process succeeds after retry with NO error surfaced (result rc 0);
- (b) a permanently held lock produces ONE actionable error after the bounded budget — the
  final failure names the lock file and includes holder/remedy guidance;
- (c) uncontended ops add no latency: `time.sleep` instrumented to record calls — zero sleeps
  on the happy path — and the advisory-lock fast path is non-blocking;
- plus: a ref-lock signature ("cannot lock ref") is retried and self-heals; two concurrent
  processes appending through the seam both succeed (advisory serialization).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The OSS research findings are recorded on this ticket and the chosen approach cites
      them rather than asserting a value (checked: research comments above; Approach cites
      §1a/§2/§4/5b per item).
- [ ] A transient index.lock or ref-lock conflict on a store git write self-heals with no
      error surfaced to the caller (behavioral test (a) + ref-lock test pass against a real
      competing lock holder).
- [ ] A permanently held lock yields exactly one actionable error naming the contended lock
      file and the remedy, after a bounded jittered budget on the order of tens of seconds
      by default (behavioral test (b) passes; message includes the lock path and guidance).
- [ ] Uncontended store git writes add no latency: no sleep on the happy path (behavioral
      test (c) passes with an instrumented `time.sleep`).
- [ ] Each local-only git call site listed in Context is either explicitly bounded with a
      watchdog justified against LOCAL latency (not copied from the network value) or
      documented as deliberately unbounded with the reason stated (checked by reading the
      five touched wrappers; `fsck.py` no longer conflicts with 01e8, which is closed).
- [ ] rebar's blocking policy under local contention is stated explicitly in
      `gitutil.py`'s module docs (bounded jittered retry + advisory serialization; silent
      transient recovery; one actionable error on a stuck lock), justified against the
      research, and applied consistently at the seam.
- [ ] make lint, make typecheck, and the targeted test files exit zero.
